chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Finger Buster and Don't You Leave Me Here
summary: Discussion of Jelly Roll's tunes, including one Caldwell did not know he composed until reading about it in Denmark.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Well, "Finger Buster" was way up tempo, wasn't it?
What was the other thing he was playing then?
Oh, let me see. He had another number there. We recorded it. This -- I didn't know that he had composed his own number around Chicago. It was "Don't you Leave Me Here, and I got a record on it.

Yes, a good -- you know, I didn't know that he composed that number until I was over in Denmark last year and happened to read it in the book. And one of the fellows got the band over there gave me the small record that was taken from the master, and he said --
He sings on it, doesn't he?
He sings on it. Yeah, that's right. That's [great]
